div.div:
interpŏsĭtus , ūs, m. (only in
I.abl. sing.), a putting between, interposition (rare but class.): “luna interpositu interjectuque terrae repente deficit,” Cic. N. D. 2, 40, 103 : “solis radios luna interpositu suo auferens terrae,” Plin. 2, 10, 7, § 47 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
